# Settings — Developers

Available on **All plans**.

## Deep links — where to find them

The Deep links block lives at **Joy Admin → Settings → Developers → Deep links** — this is the primary, canonical location. (A read-only summary also surfaces on the General settings page, but the block itself and any editing happen under **Developers**.) When a merchant asks "where are the deep links / where do I get the link", route them to **Settings → Developers**.

## Anchors (no setup needed)

- `#joy-home` — main widget home
- `#joy-ways-to-earn`
- `#joy-ways-to-redeem`
- `#joy-referral-program`

## Setup

**Shopify Admin → Online Store → Navigation → [Main menu / Footer] → Add menu item** → name (e.g., Rewards) + URL (paste `#joy-home`). Save → clicking that menu item opens the widget.

You can disable the floating widget button entirely once deeplinks are set up.

---

Available on **Advanced+**. Add/remove customer points by adding a Shopify tag.

## Enable

**Settings → Developers → Manage Tags** toggle on.

## Tag syntax

```
Joy: Add 500 - Place order #111 via POS
Joy: Subtract 100 - Refund
```

The number after Add/Subtract adjusts the balance; the comment tracks the reason.

Useful in **Shopify Flow** workflows that auto-tag customers with these strings — Joy reads tags and updates balances. Provides flexibility beyond the Joy API.

---

Use the official `joyso-hydrogen-sdk` npm package.

## Steps

1. **Joy Admin → Settings → Developers → Enable Custom Storefront development**
2. Install `joyso-hydrogen-sdk` in your Hydrogen project
3. In `app/root.jsx`: add the loader to fetch Joy data
4. Initialize Joy in root layout
5. Add CSP whitelist in `entry.server.jsx`
6. Optional CSS fix: Hydrogen quickstart uses `box-sizing: content-box` which can warp the floating button — add corrective CSS

Non-Plus stores can test with Storefront API key from a custom app in dev environment.

---

**Settings → Developers → Manage keys → Generate key** — creates App ID + Secret key.

**Important:** Generating a new key invalidates any previous key. If another app already uses the old credentials, you must update them.

**Plan required: Joy Ultimate ($499/mo) — effective September 17, 2025.**

REST API v2 and Webhook API are **exclusively available on the Ultimate plan**. Lower plans (Starter, Essential, Advanced) will receive a `PLAN_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` error.

## What's included with Ultimate API access

- **REST API v2** — manage customers, point transactions, rewards, VIP tiers, referrals
- **Webhook API** — real-time notifications for 20+ loyalty events (points earned, tier upgraded, coupon used, etc.)
- **Headless / Hydrogen** support
- Cursor-based pagination, comprehensive error handling, automatic data filtering

## Authentication

Credentials are found in **Settings → Developers → Manage keys → Generate key** (App ID + Secret Key).

Official docs: `devdocs.joy.so/joy-rest-api-v2/rest-api-v2`

## Upgrade path

**Settings → Subscription → All Plans** to upgrade to Ultimate.

---

## AI assistant connections — connect Claude / ChatGPT to Joy Loyalty

Merchants can connect an external AI assistant (e.g. **Claude**, **ChatGPT**) directly to their Joy Loyalty account so the assistant can answer questions about the loyalty program, analyze performance, and — if granted full access — take approved actions like adjusting points, tiers, and rewards on the merchant's behalf.

**Where:** **Joy Admin → Settings → Developers → AI connections** (also listed as connectable apps under **Settings → Manage keys → Read-only key**, and shown in the app's own connector picker as "Joy Loyalty").

## Two access levels

- **Read-only** — the AI assistant can view loyalty data (points, tiers, rewards, performance) but **can never change points or settings**. Recommended default for AI assistants and other read-only integrations.
- **Full access** — the AI assistant can view **and change** points, tiers, and rewards on the merchant's behalf.

## Connecting flow (OAuth-style consent)

1. The merchant starts the connection from inside the AI assistant (Claude/ChatGPT), which redirects to Joy's **consent screen**: "Connect to Joy Loyalty — *{clientName}* is requesting access."
2. Merchant reviews the requested **access level** (Read-only or Full access) and can optionally check "Remember this and skip this screen next time."
3. Merchant clicks **Allow access** (or **Deny**).
4. Once connected, the app appears under **Settings → Developers → AI connections** ("Connected apps") where the merchant can **Disconnect** it at any time — disconnecting removes access to loyalty data immediately.

## Read-only API key (separate from the existing App ID/Secret key)

In addition to the existing **Manage keys → Generate key** (App ID + Secret key, full REST API v2 access, Ultimate-only — see above), Joy now also offers a **dedicated read-only key** at **Settings → Developers → Manage keys**:
- **Generate read-only key** — creates a key that can only read data (GET requests) and can never change points. Intended for AI assistants and other read-only integrations.
- **Revoke and regenerate read-only key** — revoking immediately breaks any integration using the old key; a new key is generated in its place. This cannot be undone.

## If a merchant asks "can I connect Claude/ChatGPT to my loyalty program?"

Yes — point them to **Settings → Developers → AI connections**, and clarify the Read-only vs Full-access distinction so they choose the right scope for what they want the assistant to do.

- kb_settings-developers (Manage keys — App ID/Secret key, REST API v2)

# Analytics

Available on **Essential and above** — the Analytics page is not available on the free Starter plan. Open at **Joy Admin → Analytics**.

## Key metrics

| Metric | What it measures |
|---|---|
| **Revenue by Joy** | Revenue from orders using Joy-issued discounts |
| **Loyalty members** | Total customers who joined the program |
| **Referred revenue** | Sales generated by the referral program |
| **Redemption rate** | % of customers redeeming points (all-time) |
| **Points earned** | Total points earned by all customers |
| **Points redeemed** | Total points redeemed |

Filter by date range to track trends.

## Exporting points activity (Customer name + Order ID + Points earned)

For **point activity over a date range** (not current balances), merchants can self-serve: **Customers → Activities** → set the date range → **Export type = Earned** → enter your email → start export.

Merchants who need a report for accounting/expense reconciliation can export point-earning activity — including **Customer name, Order ID, and Points earned** together in one file. When a merchant asks for this kind of combined export, confirm the exact columns and date range they need; the data is exportable rather than a hard limitation. If the standard in-app export doesn't surface every column they need, collect the store URL + the exact fields + date range and escalate to the team to pull it.

**"Revenue by Joy" / Joy-assisted order data lives in Analytics, not Activities.** Find it at **Joy Dashboard → Analytics → Revenue by Joy** — the order table sits below the chart and can be filtered by date, with an Export button above the chart. Activities is the point-activity audit trail, a different thing.

---

Available on **Essential and above**. Joy data is recognized natively in Shopify Analytics — both **loyalty metafields** (Point Balance, VIP Tier) and **Joy tags** (engaged members, assisted orders, referral activity).

## Common reports

- **Revenue by VIP tier** — Gold contribution vs others
- **Retention by tier** — there is **no native repeat-purchase-rate-by-VIP-tier report** today (logged as feedback); use the workaround below
- **Win-back targeting** — high points + no recent order
- **Top spenders by tier** — for VIP-only campaigns
- **AOV by tier** — verify higher tiers spend more

## Requirements

- **Settings → General → Show metafields on Shopify admin** must be ON (kb_settings-general)
- For ShopifyQL: ready-made templates ship in the Joy docs — no need to write queries from scratch

## Repeat-purchase rate by tier (not native yet)

There is **no native report** for repeat-purchase rate broken down by VIP tier — it is logged as product feedback. Workaround: use the **"Returning customers – Joy active redeemers"** metric in **Shopify Analytics**, combined with **auto-tagging active redeemers** (**Settings → Additional features**). Note that **Member-Analytics** figures may be **temporarily unstable** during the current analytics revamp.

## Milestones section in the Rewards tab (AnalyticsV2)

**Joy Admin → Analytics → Rewards tab** now has a dedicated **Milestones** section showing how well milestone rewards (see kb_milestone) are performing:

- **KPI cards:** Revenue assisted (sales from orders where the customer redeemed a milestone reward in the period), Reward cost (points at exchange rate + store credit + discounts + free gifts issued as milestone rewards, added up), and Net return (Revenue assisted ÷ Reward cost — above 1× means milestone rewards are tied to more sales than they cost; below 1× is flagged).
- **Reward cost by type** — stacked bar breaking cost down by Points / Store credit / Discount / Free gift.
- **Milestone step reach** — an all-time funnel (with a program picker) showing how many customers reach each step of a milestone program.
- **Milestones reached over time** — a date-filtered line chart.
- **Milestone breakdown** — an expandable table with per-milestone detail.

This is **AnalyticsV2 only** (no equivalent on the older V1 analytics report). If a merchant reports "no milestone data" or "Milestone breakdown is empty," this can reflect a data-sync delay for store-credit/gift-card history still catching up — the UI surfaces a "Store credit & gift history still syncing" caption in that case rather than an error.

# Milestone Rewards

Available on **Advanced, Ultimate**. Set up at **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Milestones → Add milestone**.

## Milestone types

| Type | Notes |
|---|---|
| Mixed milestone *(New)* | Sequential journey combining multiple action types |
| Number of orders | Reward on Nth order (e.g. 3rd order) |
| Amount spent | Reward after spending $X total |
| Earned points | Reward after accumulating X points |
| Number of reviews | Reward on Nth review |
| Inactivity | Reward inactive customers to win them back |
| Number of referrals | Reward on Nth successful referral |
| Subscription cycles | Bonus on Nth consecutive billing cycle |

## Reward options (per milestone)

Points, Store credit, Discount amount, Discount percentage, Free gift.

Configure per milestone: name, start/end date, threshold, reward type/value.

## Milestone conditions (per rule)

- **Minimum order requirement** — No minimum / Minimum purchase amount / Minimum quantity of items
- **Anti-cheat** — Set minimum time between orders. Prevents customers from placing multiple orders within a short time frame to game the milestone. Extra orders within the window will not count toward milestones.

## Milestone settings (global)

**Progression mode** — controls what happens when a customer reaches multiple milestones at once:

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **Only the highest milestone reward** | Customer gets reward for the highest milestone reached only (e.g. if they hit milestones 1, 2, 3 at once → only reward for #3). Does not apply to Mixed milestones. |
| **All milestone rewards** | Customer gets rewards for every milestone reached (e.g. hit 1, 2, 3 at once → gets all 3 rewards). |

Path: **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Milestones → Milestone settings**

---

Tracks **consecutive successful billing cycles** across a customer's subscription contracts. Use to reduce churn and reward long-term subscribers.

## Required setup

1. Connect **Shopify Flow** at **Joy Admin → Settings → Integrations**
2. Import the Flow template **"Joy Loyalty - Subscription Order Data Sync.flow"** at **Shopify Admin → Apps → Shopify Flow → Import**, then turn it on
   - Required because Shopify doesn't natively send subscription renewal data to apps
3. Create the milestone with:
   - **Milestone condition** — N successful billing cycles
   - **Rewards** — Points, Gift, or Discount

---

Build a journey like: **"Place 3 orders → Write 2 reviews → Refer 1 friend"** — each step must be completed in order before the next unlocks.

Add via **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Milestones → Add milestone → Mixed milestone → Add milestone** for each step.

Step types available: Number of orders, Amount spent, Earned points, Number of reviews, Number of referrals.

### Naming steps and letting customers choose their reward

Each step of a Mixed milestone can be given a **custom name** (e.g. "Bronze tier", "Welcome gift") in the step editor, instead of a generic "Step 1/2/3" label — helps customers understand what each step in the journey means.

A step's reward can also be configured as a **choice of multiple rewards** rather than one fixed reward — the customer picks which reward they want when they complete that step (shown to the customer as "Choice of {rewards}"). This is set per-step alongside the existing reward type/value fields.

### Milestone progress visibility for staff (Customer Details)

Staff can see a customer's milestone progress directly on their **Joy Admin → Customers → [customer]** profile page, under a **Milestone progress** card:
- Shows progress toward the customer's next milestone, or **"All milestones reached"** if they've completed every step.
- Shows **"Reward pending"** if a reward is awaiting claim, or **"Picked: {reward}"** once the customer has chosen (for choice-of-reward steps).
- Locked steps (not yet reachable) show as **Locked**, with a **Next:** indicator for the step the customer is working toward.
- A **View milestones** link jumps to the full milestone program configuration.
- If the customer has no milestone activity yet, the card shows **"No milestone activity yet."**

# Customer Management

**Joy Admin → Customers** = the hub for after-launch ops. The grid shows:

- Name & email
- Membership type — Member / Guest / Left
- Points (active balance)
- VIP tier
- VIP point (amount contributing toward tier)
- Birthday
- Tier updated, Last updated timestamps

Search by name/email; filter by segment or tier. Click any row to open the full customer profile for point adjustments, coupon revocation, tier reassignment, and activity audit.

---

| Type | Earn | Redeem | Sees widget |
|---|---|---|---|
| Member | Yes | Yes | Full status |
| Guest | If guest earning enabled | No | General info only |
| Left program | No | No | Hidden |

## How customers become Members

- **SSO / New Customer Accounts**: customer is **always a Member** once Shopify identifies them — no separate registration needed
- **Legacy customer accounts**: customer must manually register in store
- Optional: Set all customers as Guest by default and manually approve who can join

Use **Left program** for wholesale, internal staff, test accounts, or anyone who must be excluded.

---

Quick Search bars on the **Joy homepage** and **Reward Programs page**. Search by:
- Customer email
- Order ID
- Coupon code
- Program name (on programs page)

Returns customer profile, order activities, coupon usage, redemption history.

---

## Add customer inline (Shopify Admin Intents)

In **Joy → Customers → Add customer** opens a Shopify-native modal inside Joy (uses `app.intents.invoke`). Same applies to creating/editing products and collections inside reward setup. **Requires Joy embedded mode** — not available standalone.

## Import customer data (CSV)

**Customers → Import**. Use Joy template or your own file.

**Import actions:**
- Add points to existing balances (positive adds, negative subtracts)
- Reset existing balances
- Update birthdays

**Birthday column** must be named `Birthday(MM/DD)` with format **MM/DD** (zero-padded — `03/03` correct, `3/3` wrong).

**Adjusting points does NOT change tier status** — tiers update only through VIP rules or manual tier change in customer profile.**Adjusting points does NOT change tier status** — tiers update only through VIP rules or manual tier change in customer profile.

**Import matches on email already in Shopify.** The "Non-existent customers" error means an email in the CSV does not yet exist as a Shopify customer — customers must exist in Shopify first, and the email must match exactly (no typos or extra spaces). Re-importing the same file **updates existing customers (matched by email), it does not create duplicates**, so there is no need to delete the current list first.

**Orders imported at 0 points / retro backfill.** If past orders imported without points, the team can delete and re-add points with the correct rule — confirm the date range and which customers already had manual points first, to avoid double-crediting.

**Export.** The default export may not include the **VIP tier column** — the team can enable tier in the export on request. A tier-only file can be re-imported to bulk-update tiers without touching points. A full programmatic API export is **Ultimate**.

**Accounting export (Customer Name + Order ID + Points Earned).** There is no self-serve dashboard export that combines Customer Name + Order ID + Points Earned in a single file, but the **team can generate it on request** for a given period — each line maps customer → order ID → points earned, suitable for monthly expense/accounting reporting. The native **Activities** log is the self-serve interim view in the meantime.

---

Joy syncs with **Shopify Customer Segments**. Excluded customers can't earn/redeem, don't see widget, can't access tiers/referrals.

## Setup

1. **Shopify Admin → Customers → Customer segments → Create segment** (e.g., tag "B2B")
2. Joy auto-syncs the segment
3. **Joy Admin → Settings → Pre-launch → Excluded segments** → select segments

Real-time eligibility — no manual customer-by-customer management.

## Pending Rewards tab (Customer Details)

A customer's profile (**Joy Admin → Customers → [customer]**) has a **Pending Rewards** card listing rewards the customer has qualified for but not yet claimed/used, with a status filter: **All / Pending / Claimed**.

- **Badges:** Pending, Claimed, Expired.
- Each row shows **Created** and **Expires** dates.
- **Free gift rewards awaiting product selection** show a distinct line: **"Free gift — awaiting customer product selection"** — this means the customer earned the reward but hasn't yet picked which product they want (relevant for Free gift programs with **Selection Mode**, see kb_milestone and kb_vip-tiers). This is expected, not stuck — the customer needs to open the widget/loyalty page and pick their product.
- If the list fails to load, the UI shows **"Couldn't load pending rewards — this list may be incomplete, try reloading the page"** rather than an error state; a simple page reload usually resolves it.

Use this tab to check "did this customer's reward from milestone/VIP/promo actually get issued and is it still valid" without digging through the full activity log.

# Subscription App Integrations

Joy works with **any subscription app using Shopify Selling Plans + Contracts** (the Shopify standard).

## Tested integrations

- **Joy Subscription** (deepest, native — auto-connects)
- **Shopify Subscription** (native)
- **Recharge** (auto-detected from Shopify subscription orders — discount-code sync + subscription rewards)
- Any other selling-plans-compliant app

## Two main use cases

1. **Reward subscription orders** — points for each renewal/recurring billing cycle
2. **Redeem coupons on subscription cycles** — Joy discount codes apply on subscription orders

Make sure your subscription products and selling plans are set up first.

---

## Joy Subscription

Auto-connects. **Joy Loyalty → Integrations → Joy Subscription** — shows **Connected** tag if successful. Free Advanced upgrade for Subscription if you're on Loyalty Advanced.

## Shopify Subscriptions

Install Shopify Subscriptions app first. Then **Joy Loyalty → Integrations → Shopify Subscription → Connect → Set Up** the reward program.

Both feed into the **Place subscription** earning rule (kb_earning-programs).

---

Two functions:
1. **Discount code sync** — Joy redemption coupons auto-sync to Recharge so customers apply them to subscription orders via Recharge customer portal
2. **Subscription rewards** — points awarded for subscription purchases and renewals

ReCharge is now **auto-detected from Shopify subscription orders** — there is nothing to "connect" on the Joy side. The old API-key connection (Joy Admin → Integrations → Recharge) was deprecated.

Deprecating that old API connection briefly disrupted the discount-code sync; it has since been restored and patched. If a Joy discount code is created on Shopify but does not appear on ReCharge, collect the **code + the order** so the team can verify the sync.

### "Your Recharge API token needs an additional permission" error

If the merchant sees this error, it's specifically about **bulk-issued reward codes** (e.g. a VIP tier relaunch that issues rewards to many customers at once) failing to sync to Recharge — **not** the regular one-at-a-time discount-code sync. Cause: their Recharge API token is missing the **`write_batches`** permission.

**Fix:** the merchant edits their API token in the **Recharge admin** to add the `write_batches` permission, then retries. This is a Recharge-side permission, not a Joy setting — Joy can't grant it on the merchant's behalf.

## Subscription renewals from non-native apps need the Flow bridge

Shopify does not natively pass subscription **renewal** data to apps. For subscription apps that are not natively integrated (e.g. Seal, BOLD, Subi), connect **Shopify Flow** (Settings → Integrations) and import the **"Joy Loyalty - Subscription Order Data Sync.flow"** template — then renewals earn points like one-time orders. See kb_milestone and kb_integrations-shopify-flow.

# Redeeming Programs

Set up at **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Redeeming programs**.

> Plan names below use current naming: **Starter** (free), **Essential**, **Advanced**, **Ultimate**. "Pro" is the legacy name for **Essential** — if any older material says "Pro", read it as Essential.

| Program | Plans |
|---|---|
| Discount (amount, %, BXGY) | All |
| Free gift | Essential, Advanced, Ultimate |
| Free shipping | Essential, Advanced, Ultimate |
| Gift Card | Essential, Advanced, Ultimate |
| Coupon list at checkout | Ultimate (Shopify Plus + Checkout Extensibility) |
| Redeem at checkout page | Ultimate (Shopify Plus + Checkout Extensibility); Advanced via sales contact |
| Total/per-customer redemption limits | All |

When customers redeem, Joy generates a unique one-time-use coupon code.

## How customers actually redeem

The main path is the widget or loyalty page: the customer logs in, opens the widget, goes to **Redeem points**, picks a reward and clicks **Redeem**. They then either click **Apply** to push the code to the cart, or copy the code and paste it at checkout.

**The code does not apply itself at checkout.** This is the single most common "my discount vanished" report — points were spent, the code was issued and is valid, but nobody entered it. Unused codes are always retrievable from the widget's **My coupons** section.

Other redemption surfaces: the **cart drawer** (kb_cart-drawer), **checkout page** (Quick Redeem / coupon list / redeem-at-checkout, see below), and **POS** (staff look up the balance and apply the reward to the cart).

One quirk: if a customer clicks Apply while their cart is empty, the discount is held and takes effect once items are added — the page may need a refresh before the cart reflects it.

**Minimum order value is checked at the moment the coupon is applied at checkout, not at redemption.** So a customer can redeem anytime, but the discount only takes effect once their cart reaches the minimum. Joy displays the minimum automatically wherever the reward appears — e.g. "Applicable for $85 minimum orders" — on the widget, loyalty page, and again in the coupon details under My Rewards after redemption; the condition is never hidden. For Free Gift rewards, merchants can also add their own description to a reward, shown on the widget and loyalty page.

**A redeemed reward is an order-level discount, applied once per order regardless of item quantity.** A merchant with 2+ units of a product in the cart will see the same discount amount as with 1 unit — there is no per-unit multiplication or per-unit cap on a redeemed reward's value. This is expected behaviour, not a bug.

---

## Discount types

- **Discount amount** — fixed $ off
- **Discount percentage** — % off
- **Buy X Get Y (BXGY)** — buy quantity → get extra products/discounts

## Redeem value modes

- **Dynamic Discount** — flexible point thresholds. Optional limits:
  - Minimum points required to redeem
  - Maximum points per redemption
  - Maximum discount % of cart total
- **Fixed Discount** — set $ amount per redemption

## Settings

- **Applicable categories** — products/collections discount applies to
- **Minimum order requirement** — cart minimum
- **Coupon expiration date** — when an individual generated code expires (separate from the reward's own Start/End date, see below)
- **Combinations** — which Shopify discount classes can stack
- **Sales channels** — where the discount is valid

## Redemption program Start/End date

Every redemption program (discount, free gift, free shipping, gift card, etc.) has a **Start/End date** setting, with a **"No end date"** toggle that is **on by default** — existing reward programs keep working unchanged unless a merchant explicitly sets an end date.

- **Start date** — the reward isn't offered for redemption before this date.
- **End date** — once it passes, the reward **automatically hides from new redemption** (customers can no longer redeem it). This is separate from a code's own **Coupon expiration date**: codes customers **already claimed before the end date remain valid** and usable until their own individual expiry — an expired program end date does not retroactively invalidate codes already in customers' hands.
- This is an extension of the older "coupon expiration date" concept: coupon expiration controls when an issued code expires, while Start/End date controls when the reward itself is available to be redeemed at all.

## Reward visibility when restricted to a Shopify customer segment

When a redemption program's **"Who can use this reward"** is set to a specific **Shopify customer segment**, the reward is now **fully hidden from ineligible customers** — it does not appear on the widget, loyalty page, or storefront for anyone outside the segment.

**This is a behavior change.** Previously, a segment-restricted reward was still visible to everyone but blocked/unusable for customers outside the segment. If a merchant or a confused customer asks why a reward "disappeared" even though it used to show up, this is expected: the reward is working as intended, just now hidden instead of shown-but-blocked for non-eligible customers.

---

Available on Essential, Advanced, Ultimate.

## Selection modes

- **Free one product from selection** (default) — customer picks one
- **Free all products in selection** — useful for bundles

**Only products published to the Online Store sales channel sync to Joy and appear in the reward product picker.** Products left as Draft, or removed from the Online Store channel, won't be selectable. If a merchant wants a reward product that shouldn't be publicly browsable: keep the product **Active** in Shopify (it must stay Active for the program to reference it) but hide the Buy button — group reward products under a dedicated product template and hide the Buy button on that template — or combine with a VIP tier perk (**Membership → VIP Tiers → [tier] → Tier privileges → Exclusive products/collections**) to restrict purchase while still allowing point redemption.

### "Too many products/variants" error on a discount program
If a merchant hits a discount-selection limit error even though they picked fewer than 100 **products**, the limit actually counts **variants**, not products — a handful of multi-variant products can add up to 100+ variants quickly. This is a hard cap from **Shopify's own Discount API**, not a Joy setting, and Joy can't raise it. Workaround: group the products into a Shopify **Collection** and select the collection instead of individual products/variants.

## Variants

- For multi-variant products, you can mark specific variants or all as eligible
- If multiple eligible variants are in cart, discount applies to the **lowest-priced variant** automatically

## Settings

Discount combinations, sales channels, usage restrictions (everyone vs only redeemer), coupon expiration, refund-on-cancel, custom code prefix.

Customers select the product in the loyalty widget when redeeming.

---

Essential, Advanced, Ultimate. Same setup as discount: points cost, minimum order, combinations (stack with order/product discounts), sales channels, expiration, refund-on-cancel.

Unused coupons can be revoked and converted back to points by merchant on customer request — **Joy Admin → Customers → [name] → Revoke coupon**.

**Once a coupon has been generated, its conditions and expiry cannot be edited.** If a customer's coupon is about to expire or has expired, the practical fix is to issue a replacement discount code — either revoke and let them re-redeem, or create a code directly in Shopify Admin → Discounts. Expired coupons are automatically hidden from the widget, so customers won't see dead codes.

**Note: changing Combinations only affects newly issued coupons** — codes already in customers' hands keep the settings they were created with.

### Deactivate a coupon WITHOUT refunding points

**Revoke** always converts the unused coupon **back into points** — that is by design, and there is no toggle to "revoke without refund" and no bulk-deactivate in Joy.

- To **disable a code but keep the points spent**, deactivate the code **directly in Shopify → Discounts** (do **not** use Joy's Revoke). Note: after deactivating in Shopify, the coupon's status inside Joy may not auto-update to Expired — if the merchant needs the app status synced, escalate.
- To **deactivate many/all coupons at once without refunding** (e.g. before re-launching a new redeem program), there is no self-serve UI — escalate with the store URL and the list/criteria of coupons to disable. Append `<escalate_human>`.

---

## Gift Card redeem program

Available on Essential, Advanced, Ultimate.

A **Gift Card** redeem program lets customers exchange points for a **real, reusable Shopify gift card** — not a one-time-use coupon like the other redeem types. The card has its own **balance** and can be spent down gradually across **multiple orders**, just like any gift card issued directly in Shopify.

- **Setup:** **Reward programs → create redeem program → choose type "Gift Card"**. The first time a merchant sets this up, Joy requires granting the app **gift-card permission** in Shopify before the program can be created.
- **On redeem:** the customer can choose to keep the gift card for themselves, or enter a friend's email to send it directly to that person — Shopify sends the gift card to the recipient.
- **Code visibility (security):** the **full gift card code is shown only once**, at the moment of issuance. After that, only the **last 4 digits** are visible — including to the store owner in Shopify Admin. This matches Shopify's own standard gift-card behavior and is not a Joy-specific limitation.

## Send Gift to a Friend (Free Gift rewards)

After a customer redeems a **Free Gift** reward, they get a **"Send to a friend"** option that lets them send the gift coupon directly to someone else — entering the friend's email, name, and a message — instead of, or in addition to, keeping it for themselves.

- **Enable at:** Free Gift program → turn on "Send to Friend" and choose a delivery/automation method.
- **Delivery methods (3):** Joy's built-in email, **Shopify Flow**, or **Klaviyo** — same automation options as Referral. For Joy's built-in email, the template is under **Settings → Notifications → "Send gift to friend"**.
- **Where it appears:** the main widget, loyalty page, My Rewards, and Customer Account.
- **Rate limit (Joy in-app sending only):** fixed at **100 emails/day** total and **1 recipient per 24 hours**, to prevent spam/abuse. This limit is **not merchant-configurable**.

---

Both require **Shopify Plus + Checkout Extensibility** and **Ultimate** plan (Advanced via sales contact).

## Coupon list at checkout

Shows previously redeemed unused coupons inline at checkout. Customer applies in one click. Add via **Reward programs → Redeem programs → [program] → Set up here → Add app block → Joy Coupon List**.

## Redeem at checkout page

Lets customer convert points to discount **directly at checkout**, no widget needed. Toggle on in the program's Redeem value section. Cancel = points refunded instantly.

**Limitation:** Checkout UI extensions don't support i18n by IP/browser. Theme Editor lets you set one main language only.

---

In each program's **Redemption limit** card:
- **Program total limitation** — overall cap (e.g. 50)
- **Each customer's limit** — per-customer cap (optional)

Whichever cap hits first stops further redemptions. When total limit is reached, reward shows **Sold out** in widget. Reset manually via the Reset button next to the counter (cannot be undone). Limits can be edited live without affecting existing redemptions. Only completed redeems count.

## Per-customer limit uses a rolling window (known limitation)
The per-customer / daily redemption limit counts time as a **rolling 24-hour cycle**, not a reset at the store timezone's midnight. So a customer who redeems at 5pm stays locked until 5pm the next day, not until midnight. This can feel unexpected (e.g. locked out at 10am the morning after an evening purchase). There is currently **no merchant-facing setting to switch to a midnight reset** — this is logged product feedback under review by the team. Don't promise a fix date; acknowledge it as a known limitation.

## "Reward program(s) need attention" warning banner

Joy Admin shows a warning banner (e.g. "**{count} reward program(s) need attention**") when a reward program's underlying **product or collection reference is broken**:

- **Unavailable products/collections** — the program references a product or collection that's been deleted, unpublished from Online Store, or otherwise no longer available in Shopify. Message: `"{programTitle}" references products or collections that are no longer available: {productTitles}`.
- **Out of stock** — products referenced by the program (e.g. a Free gift program) are out of stock. Message: `Products in "{programTitle}" are out of stock: {productTitles}`.

Each flagged item has a **Review this reward** link that jumps straight to the program's settings so the merchant can swap in a new product/collection or restock. This surfaces the same underlying constraint already documented above ("only products published to the Online Store sales channel sync to Joy and appear in the reward product picker") — the banner is Joy proactively catching it instead of the merchant discovering it when a customer can't redeem.

# Loyalty Widget & Branding

## Classic widget vs Unified widget

Joy launched the **Unified widget** as a complete rebuild of the storefront loyalty UI.

| | Classic widget | Unified widget |
|---|---|---|
| **Who has it** | Merchants who installed Joy before the Unified launch | Merchants who installed Joy after the Unified widget launch |
| **Status badge** | "Classic is live" | "Unified widget — Live" |
| **Focus** | Points and rewards only | All-in-one: profile, orders, wishlist, recommendations, points, rewards, and more |
| **Design editor** | 4 horizontal tabs (Widget theme / Membership card / Display / Advanced) | Full sidebar editor with live storefront preview |
| **Customization** | Limited color/font options | Every color, font, spacing, border radius exposed as CSS properties — full brand control |
| **Performance** | Standard | Lazy-loaded, smaller bundle on first paint |
| **Data** | — | Same Joy data — programs, points, customers carry over untouched |

## How to check which widget you're on

**Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design** section — it shows two cards, **Unified widget** and **Classic widget**:
- Badge says **"Classic is live"** → you're on Classic
- Badge says **"Unified is live"** on the Unified card → you're on Unified

## Switching from Classic to Unified

Merchants on Classic can switch at any time:
- **Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Switch to Unified** button (at the Widget design section heading)
- All existing Joy data (points, programs, customers) carries over — nothing is lost
- Both versions never run simultaneously

## Free setup offer

When a merchant asks about the difference or expresses interest in switching, offer the free setup service:

> "We're offering a free setup service where our team styles your unified loyalty widget or loyalty page to match your store's branding, colors, layout — the whole thing. You won't need to lift a finger. We'll take care of it and send you the result to review. Do you want to give it a try?"

If merchant accepts → collect store URL and escalate to team with `<escalate_human>`.

## Classic widget — features still on Classic only

Milestone program UI, interactive website popup, Wallet pass / QR, Submit receipt program, branded reminder popup — these auto-fallback to Classic UI even on Unified stores.

---

## How to identify Widget v4

The easiest tell: go to **Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Setup**. 
- **V4**: opens a full **Widget design editor** with a left sidebar (Settings / Header / Body / Footer / Extensions / Advanced) and a live storefront preview on the right.
- **V3**: opens a page with 4 horizontal tabs (Widget theme / Membership card / Display / Advanced settings).

## Widget design editor — path

**Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Setup**

## Sidebar structure

### Settings
- **Design** — Preset Theme (Midnight, Forest, Ocean, Warm, Blush, Minimal, Dark, Slate) + Industry inspiration presets (Fashion, Beauty & Wellness, Food & Drink, Home & Garden, Sports & Fitness, Pets & Animals, Men's Grooming, Default), Primary color, Background color, Layout (Widget / Drawer), Position on desktop, Earn & Redeem layout (Tabs / Separate blocks), Text size, Border radius (None / Sharp / Soft / Rounded / Extra), Currency icon (None / Emoji / Image), Fonts (Heading + Body), Text theme colors, Buttons (color, text color, text case), Cards (heading/body text color, background, border)
- **Launcher** — Float button style (Icon only / Label only / Icon & label / Point balance), Point balance label, Label section color, Button size (S/M/L/XL), Border radius (Pill/Rounded/Square), Alignment (Bottom left / Bottom right)
- **Content & Translations** — inline editor to customize all widget text labels (Program name, Launcher, Guest view, Logged in, Points display, Tier perks, Program tabs, Section titles, Coupons, Referral, Redeem flow, Earn flow, bundle chip templates like `Save {{value}} · {{type}}`, etc.). Buttons: **Revert to default** (reset all text) and **On-brand** (AI-rewrite labels to match store voice).

### Header
- **Header** — Program name text size (Small/Medium/Large), Header background color (or "Use primary"), Header text color, Logo (Add image, or paste image URL, or "Use store logo" button — any aspect ratio, height configurable), Header background image (upload; recommended **8:5 ratio, 800×500px, under 200KB**) + overlay opacity slider

### Body
Each block can be **toggled on/off** and **drag-and-drop reordered**. Click any block to edit its content, text, or images inline.

| Block | Notes |
|---|---|
| Membership card | Card layout (Compact/Classic), Default avatar, Guest card image, Member card image, Sign-in settings, Open widget after login |
| My coupons | — |
| Refer a friend | — |
| Ways to earn | — |
| Ways to redeem | — |
| Recently viewed | Off by default |
| Recommended | Off by default |
| Recent activity | Off by default |
| Milestones | — |
| My QR code | — |
| Wallet pass | — |
| Subscription portal | Requires Joy Subscription extension |
| Wishlist | Off by default; works with **Joy Wishlist**, and also auto-detects **Swym Wishlist Plus** or **Wishlist King** if the store has one of those installed instead — no extra config needed to switch provider |

**Membership card custom blocks** — click the `+` under Membership card to add: Heading, Rich text, Button, Divider, Image banner, Image with text, Custom link, Custom CTA.

### Footer
- **Footer menu** — bottom navigation tabs. Drag to reorder, toggle visibility, customize each tab.
  - **Display mode**: Icons & labels / Icons only / Labels only
  - **Active indicator style**: Pill / (others)
  - Tabs: **Home, Rewards, Orders, Wishlist, Reviews, Profile** (each toggleable; Wishlist/Reviews hidden by default)
- **Profile** (the Profile tab's sub-pages, each toggleable): Account info, Referral link, Social accounts, Shipping addresses, Settings, Log out, Reviews. The **Settings** sub-page includes SMS/WhatsApp marketing consent — see "SMS/WhatsApp marketing consent in Profile" below.

## SMS/WhatsApp marketing consent in Profile

The Unified widget's **Profile → Settings** sub-page lets customers opt in to SMS/WhatsApp marketing directly from the widget, without leaving the storefront.

- **Where:** Widget → **Profile → Settings**.
- **Flow:** the customer enters their phone number and toggles consent to receive SMS/WhatsApp messages. If the customer has no phone number on file yet, they first see an **"Add your phone"** prompt in Account info — once a number is saved, the consent toggle becomes available.
- **What Joy does:** Joy writes the consent to the customer's record on **Shopify**, so the merchant can use it for marketing/automation (e.g. segments, flows).
- **What Joy does NOT do:** Joy does not send the SMS/WhatsApp messages itself — actual sending still goes through whatever SMS/WhatsApp platform the merchant already has connected. Joy's role here is only to capture and store the consent.

### Extensions
Toggle on/off: **Wishlist**, **Bundling**, **Reviews**, **Subscription**, **Survey**. Each extension that needs a companion app (e.g. Wishlist) shows an "Install app / Watch setup guide / Verify installation" panel and a layout/options block (e.g. Wishlist layout: Carousel / Grid / List, image hover effect). The Wishlist extension auto-detects **Joy Wishlist**, **Swym Wishlist Plus**, or **Wishlist King** — whichever wishlist app the store has installed — with no extra config needed to pick the provider.

### Advanced
- **Display** — hide widget from guests, page restriction, instant popup, hide widget button
- **Popup** — popup behavior settings
- **Custom links** — redirect links for earning programs
- **Custom CSS** — custom CSS field for pixel-level overrides
- **External discounts** — off by default; shows up to 10 external (non-Joy) discount codes inside the widget's My Coupons block. See "Show External Discounts in My Coupons" below.

## Show External Discounts in My Coupons

Joy can surface discount codes that were **not created by Joy** — e.g. codes made directly in Shopify, or by another app like Klaviyo — inside the widget's **My Coupons** section, next to the customer's regular Joy coupons. This solves the case where a merchant wants a non-Joy discount to be visible to customers in the loyalty widget.

- **Where to enable:** Widget design editor → **Advanced → External discounts**.
- **Default:** off.
- **Limit:** the merchant selects up to **10** discount codes to show.
- **Eligibility:** Joy only displays a selected code to customers who actually qualify for it (matching the discount's own audience — All customers / Specific customers / Segment — and whether it's still within its active dates and usage limit). Each visible code shows its value and conditions.
- This is a Unified widget feature; it lives in the same Advanced tab as Display/Popup/Custom CSS settings.

## Live preview controls

The editor's right pane is a live storefront preview with an **"Embed active"** status badge. The "Preview as" toolbar lets the merchant simulate different viewers without affecting the live store:
- **Device** — Desktop / Mobile
- **Customer** — Signed in / Guest
- **VIP tier** — Member (no VIP) / Simulate VIP active
- **Customise customer data…** — set sample points/tier for the preview
- **View on store** — open the real storefront in a new tab

## How to change/replace images

A preset theme (or industry inspiration) only sets **sample images** — it never locks them. To use your own images, you edit each image where it lives, block by block; there is no single "images" page.

**Steps:**
1. Open **Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Setup**.
2. In the left sidebar, navigate to Sections ⛶,  click the **Header** or the **Body block** that contains the image you want to change (e.g. Header logo, Header background image, Membership card → Default avatar / Guest card / Member card image, or an Image banner / Image with text custom block) (https://capture.avada.io/i/3MlO1vlvJ8z3).
3. In the editor (middle pane), find that image's field and click **Upload image** (or paste an image URL) to replace it. The live preview on the right updates immediately.
4. **Save.**

**Where images live:**

| Image | Where to change it |
|---|---|
| Program logo | Header → Logo (Add image / paste URL / Use store logo) |

> **"Your Logo" placeholder showing instead of the store's logo:** this is expected, not a bug. When no image has been uploaded to the Header → Logo field, Joy displays a default **"Your Logo"** placeholder there. The fix is simply to upload a logo (or click **Use store logo**) at **Header → Logo** — no need to escalate.
| Header background | Header → Header background image (8:5, 800×500px, <200KB) |
| Default avatar (no uploaded avatar) | Body → Membership card → Default avatar (1:1, 200×200px, <200KB) |
| Guest card banner | Body → Membership card → Guest card |
| Member card banner | Body → Membership card → Member card image |
| Custom image block | Body → Membership card → `+` → Image banner / Image with text |

> Tip: the banner shown inside the membership card in the preview (e.g. the "Fuel your adventure" image) is a Membership card image block — click Membership card to swap it.

## Display & Popup settings (page restriction, hide widget) — all plans

All these settings are available on **every plan, including Starter (free)** — there is no plan restriction on them. Both live under **Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Setup → Advanced**, but on two different sidebar tabs:

**Advanced → Display:**
- **Hide widget from guests** (also labeled **"Display after login"** in the Unified widget V4 editor — same toggle, turning it on means the widget only shows to logged-in/identified customers and stays hidden for guests/non-logged-in visitors) — only show the widget to logged-in customers.
- **Hide widget button** — turn off to always display the widget button.

**Advanced → Popup:**
- **Instant popup** — Off by default; enable to let the widget open automatically when customers visit the store.
- **Page restriction** ("Show on specific pages") — Off by default (widget shows on all pages). Toggle on, then check the pages to show on: Home page, Product pages, Collection pages, Cart pages, Blog pages, Custom page.

> Common mistake: "Show on specific pages" is **not** under Display — it's under **Popup**, alongside Instant popup.

## Brand colors

Joy auto-detects your store's primary, secondary, accent palette. Edit at **Joy Admin → Settings → Colors**. These appear in color pickers throughout Joy.

## Display types

- **Floating widget** — small chatbox-style button (default)
- **Drawer** — large side panel similar to cart drawer
- Mobile slides up from bottom for both

## Setup path

**Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Setup** — controls layout, color, position, advanced custom CSS.

## Safe preview

Duplicate your theme in Shopify, enable the Joy app embed on the duplicate, and use Shopify's Preview to test without affecting live customers.

## Enable on storefront

**Theme Editor → App Embeds → Joy Loyalty - Widget → Save**.

---

| Method | New customer accounts | Shopify Plus + Legacy | Setup |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sign in with Shop App | ✅ | ✅ | Toggle only |
| Email OTP | ❌ | ✅ | Paste Multipass key |
| Sign in with Google | ❌ | ✅ | Toggle only |
| Sign in with Facebook | ❌ | ✅ | Toggle only |

If your store uses **new customer accounts**, only Shop App login appears. Email OTP, Google, Facebook need Shopify Plus + legacy accounts and use Multipass.

## Setup

**Joy Admin → Settings → Additional Features → toggle Sign in with Shop App** (or other methods).

---

All in **Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Setup**.

## Referral popup

Customizable popups: **Referral Popup** (invite), **Referral Rewards Popup** (reward messaging), **Referral Success Popup**. Choose template or custom; configure content, position, frequency. If you skip the dedicated referral floating button, customers still access referral via the main widget.

## Visit website popup

Strategic on-arrival nudge. Configure two states: **Before Sign-In** and **After Sign-In**. Customize button icon, position (e.g., bottom-right).

## Reward reminder

Auto pop-ups when customer has unused/qualifying rewards.

**Path:** Joy Admin → On-site content → **Popups** → Reward reminder → Setup. (The Popups tab is a top-level tab of On-site content — there is **no** "Branding" step. The reward reminder is a legacy block being deprecated; on Unified/V4 shops it's folded into the widget and the Popups tab only shows while the shop still has these blocks.)

| Reminder | Trigger |
|---|---|
| Birthday reward | Birthday approaching/today |
| Milestone achieved | Reached a new milestone |
| Unused discount | Has unredeemed coupon |
| Reward redemption | Has enough points |
| Visit website | Visits the store |

The Reward reminder Setup screen only configures **when/how the reminder pops up** (trigger, display mode, text). It does **NOT** have an image-upload field.

> **Changing the images shown in a reward reminder / membership card popup:** those images are NOT edited in the Popups tab. They are Membership card images inside the widget editor. Route the merchant to **On-site content → Widget → Widget design → open the editor → Sections → Membership card → Guest card image / Member card image → Upload image** (see "How to change/replace images" above). This is the correct fix when a merchant says the reward/reminder popup "still shows the stock/sample image."

## Display modes

- **Show highest priority only** (default) — drag to reorder priority list
- **Show all sequentially** — one after another, each dismissed per session

## Membership card — show store credit instead of points

For stores that **only use Shopify store credit** (see kb_points-advanced) and don't run a points program, the Membership card block has a toggle to show the **store credit balance** in place of the points balance, and hide the separate balance section.

**Where:** **On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Setup → Body → Membership card**.

**What this changes across the storefront when enabled:**
- The membership card shows store credit balance instead of points.
- **If the store no longer awards or accepts points at all**, points are hidden not just on the widget but also on the **customer account page** and the **Loyalty Hub**, wherever the store credit balance takes their place.
- **If the store still has any points program active**, both the customer account page and the Loyalty Hub keep showing points as normal — this toggle only fully hides points once no points program is running.

If a merchant on a store-credit-only setup asks why points still show somewhere, check whether they still have an active points-earning program running — that's the deciding factor, not just this toggle.

# Translations

## Plan availability

| Feature | Plans |
|---|---|
| Edit English content | All |
| Change default language + edit content | All (including Free) |
| Detect Language tab (view-only — see detected language per visitor) | All |
| Add languages (add additional languages beyond the default) | Essential, Advanced, Ultimate |

## Surfaces translated

- Loyalty widget (popup) ✅
- Loyalty page (embedded) ✅
- Account page (Loyalty Hub) ✅
- Checkout page (Shopify checkout extensions) ✅
- Apple Wallet & Google Wallet passes ✅

Joy stands out by translating **checkout extensions and customer account UI** — many other loyalty apps cannot.

## Coverage

38 supported languages, all fully customizable — every label, message, button text editable to match brand voice.

---

## Setup

**Joy Admin → Settings → Translations** → choose default language (available on all plans, including Free). The **Detected Language** tab is visible on all plans (view-only — shows detected language by IP/browser per visitor). Adding additional languages beyond the default requires Essential plan or above.

### Detected Language — no cap on number of languages

The Detected Language list has no limit on how many languages can appear — a previous cap of 5 detected languages has been removed, so merchants selling across many markets (e.g. EU) can have as many as needed detected/added.

## Editing

Pick the language → edit any label/message/button per surface. Save. Updates apply to live storefront immediately.

### Editing widget text specifically (e.g. "Membership card", "Receive exclusive offers...")

Two routes reach the same underlying widget strings — either works:

- **Settings → Translations** → pick language → **Widget design** surface → pick the block (e.g. **Membership card**) → edit the label text.
- **On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Setup** (the widget editor) → left sidebar **Settings → Content & Translations** — inline editor for all widget text labels, with **Revert to default** and **On-brand** (AI-rewrite) buttons.

If the merchant is asking about wording, not styling, either path fixes it — no design/CSS change needed.

## Known limitations

- Translations entered on the **Classic** widget carry over when switching to **Unified** — no re-entry needed.
- Some strings, specifically **VIP tier descriptions inside Customer Accounts**, can show untranslated and may need manual entry; log a gap if a surface won't translate.
- **Redeem-reward product names cannot be translated through Joy.** When a reward is tied to a specific Shopify product, the name shown to customers is pulled directly from that product's title in Shopify — it isn't a Joy-editable label. To show it in another language, translate the product's title itself (e.g. via Shopify's own product-title translation / Translate & Adapt on the product), not through Joy's Translations settings.

## Checkout limitation

Shopify Checkout UI extensions don't support i18n by IP/browser. You can only set **one default language** at the checkout level via Theme Editor. The rest of Joy (widget, loyalty page, account page) supports auto-detect normally.

## AI text-edit assistant — editing widget labels by prompt

Inside the widget text editor (**On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Setup → left sidebar → Settings → Content & Translations**), the **On-brand (AI-rewrite)** tool works as a conversational assistant: the merchant types a plain-language request (e.g. *"make the Earn button say Get rewards"*) and the assistant proposes the matching label change(s).

- **Scope:** this assistant **only edits widget text** — for styling/layout use the widget design settings, and for anything outside the widget (e.g. broader loyalty program questions) it points the merchant to the **main Joy AI assistant** instead.
- **Multiple matches:** if the request could match more than one label, the assistant lets the merchant **choose which one(s) to change** before applying.
- **Dynamic values are protected:** if a label contains a dynamic variable (e.g. the points number), the assistant won't produce a rewording that drops the variable — it'll ask the merchant to keep it in the new wording.
- **Exact wording needed:** if the merchant references text that doesn't match anything in the widget's current labels, the assistant reports it can't find that text and asks them to paste the exact wording as it appears on the widget.
- **Language-scoped:** the assistant only edits the language tab that's currently open — if the merchant wants the same change in another language, they need to switch to that language's tab first and ask again.
